notes: One of the oldest and most revered shrines in Japan; worshippers clap four times rather than two.

details.history: Of mythic antiquity, the shrine is tied in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki to the kuni-yuzuri, the ceding of the land by Okuninushi to the heavenly deities, in return for which the great shrine was built.
details.why_visit: The towering honden and the colossal shimenawa rope of the Kagura-den make Izumo unforgettable; it is the foremost shrine of enmusubi, the binding of good relationships.
details.prayer_focus: Matchmaking and good relationships (縁結び), good marriage, and fortune.
details.best_season: The 10th lunar month — known elsewhere as Kannazuki (month without gods) but at Izumo as Kamiarizuki, the month the gods gather here.

deities.role: Principal deity (主祭神); kami of nation-building and of binding relationships.
deities.regional_lore: At Izumo, Okuninushi is honored as the builder of the land who ceded it to the heavenly grandchild (kuni-yuzuri) and withdrew into the unseen realm of relationships and fate; from this he became the great matchmaking kami, said to convene the assembled gods each autumn to decide the year's unions.

canonical.canonical_lore: A descendant of Susanoo who, with Sukunabikona, pacified and developed the land of Izumo before ceding it to the heavenly deities. (Kojiki / Nihon Shoki)

events.time_prose: The 10th lunar month (Kamiarizuki) — in 2026, late November. Dates set annually by the lunar calendar.
events.origin: When the myriad gods of Japan are believed to leave their own shrines and gather at Izumo to deliberate on human affairs and relationships.
events.meaning: A solemn reception of the assembled deities and a petition for auspicious bonds in the coming year.
events.ritual: The Karasade rites welcome and later send off the gods; the shrine observes strict quiet during the divine assembly.
events.prayer: For good relationships and fortunate unions.
events.visitor_notes: The most spiritually charged period at Izumo; visitors are asked to keep a reverent quiet during the rites.
